prohibited_recommendations: Do not treat with corticosteroids: oral corticosteroids are strongly advised against and IV methylprednisolone is not recommended [EAN_PNS_2023].
Do not give IVIg directly after plasma exchange, and do not give a second IVIg course [EAN_PNS_2023, Walgaard_2021].
Do not start IVIg without checking renal function.
Do not use succinylcholine for intubation: denervated muscle risks severe hyperkalaemia.
required_recommendations: Admit to the ICU and intubate electively: FVC has fallen from 1.8 to 1.4 L (17.1 mL/kg, below 20 mL/kg), MIP is -22 cmH2O (weaker than -30), MEP 34 cmH2O (below 40), PaCO2 is 48 mmHg, and he has bulbar weakness with dysphagia and a weak cough [Lawn_2001, EAN_PNS_2023].
Start IVIg 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (2 g/kg total, about 33 g/day at 82 kg) or plasma exchange 200-250 mL/kg over 5 sessions: he cannot walk and is 5 days from onset [EAN_PNS_2023].
Continuous cardiac telemetry with blood pressure monitoring; treat symptomatic bradyarrhythmias.
Nil by mouth until a formal swallow assessment (dysphagia for thin liquids).

avoided_actions.rationale: GBS is a peripheral nerve / nerve-root disorder; EEG has no role in diagnosis unless atypical CNS features (encephalopathy, seizures) are present.
Echocardiography is not indicated in typical GBS; reserve for pre-existing cardiac disease or unexplained hemodynamic instability after autonomic causes are excluded.
Head CT contributes no diagnostic information in GBS; the disease is peripheral and CT does not visualise nerve roots reliably.
Brain MRI is reserved for atypical features (encephalopathy, CNS signs, transverse myelitis on differential). In classic GBS it does not aid diagnosis.

accepted: Guillain-Barré syndrome, severe AIDP requiring mechanical ventilation (post-Campylobacter)

differential.key_features: Cannot be excluded at presentation: 5 days of progression fits GBS; reconsider if progression continues beyond 8 weeks or treatment-related fluctuations recur.

differential.diagnosis: Acute motor axonal neuropathy (axonal GBS subtype)
differential.key_features: Campylobacter is a common antecedent of AMAN, but he has sensory symptoms and absent SNAPs, and the NCS shows prolonged latencies and slowed conduction in the demyelinating range.
Weakness ascended from the legs after distal paraesthesias, with sensory loss, areflexia and a demyelinating NCS; botulism is descending and purely motor.
Community onset with no preceding critical illness.
No tick exposure; sensory involvement and a raised CSF protein are not features of tick paralysis.

key_clinical_evidence: Rapidly ascending four-limb weakness with global areflexia and facial diplegia after culture-confirmed Campylobacter enteritis, with CSF albuminocytological dissociation (protein 124 mg/dL, 2 cells/mm3) and a demyelinating NCS, meets Brighton level 1 [Brighton_2011].

FVC below 20 mL/kg and falling, MIP weaker than -30 cmH2O, MEP below 40 cmH2O, hypercapnia and bulbar weakness together call for elective intubation; the decision rests on the trend, bulbar function, cough and fatigue, not one threshold [Lawn_2001, EAN_PNS_2023].

The antecedent infection is a history finding; serology is not needed for the diagnosis, and a positive IgM does not prove the trigger. A preceding diarrhoeal illness counts toward a poorer predicted outcome in the modified Erasmus GBS Outcome Score [Walgaard_2011].
Autonomic instability (bradyarrhythmia, blood pressure lability) is a leading cause of death in severe GBS; continuous monitoring is kept while weakness progresses [EAN_PNS_2023].

results.finding: Guidelines for adults with GBS who cannot walk unaided advise IVIg 2 g/kg over 5 days within 2 weeks of onset or plasma exchange within 4 weeks, with no preference between them; corticosteroids are not advised.
A second IVIg course in patients with a poor predicted prognosis did not improve outcome and caused more serious adverse events.

general.summary: IVIg or plasma exchange is advised for adults with GBS unable to walk unaided; neither is preferred, and a second IVIg course is not advised [EAN_PNS_2023, Walgaard_2021].

specialized_test.impression: Severe acute demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy. Markedly prolonged distal motor latencies, severely reduced conduction velocities with reduced CMAP amplitudes, absent F-waves and H-reflexes, absent sensory SNAPs bilaterally. Needle EMG: reduced recruitment without active denervation. Findings meet electrodiagnostic criteria for acute demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy. Clinical correlation recommended.

quantitative_data.pattern: Severe acquired demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy: markedly prolonged distal motor latencies, severely reduced conduction velocities, reduced CMAP amplitudes, absent F-waves, H-reflexes and SNAPs

patient.chief_complaint: Five-day rapidly progressive ascending leg weakness and areflexia with bilateral facial diplegia, preceded by Campylobacter gastroenteritis 2 weeks ago. Unable to walk. Respiratory function declining.
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. W. is a 35-year-old physical therapist presenting with a 5-day history of rapidly progressive neurological symptoms. Two weeks before admission, he had confirmed Campylobacter jejuni gastroenteritis (stool culture positive at an urgent care clinic) lasting 4 days. He recovered, and 5 days ago, 9 days after the diarrhoea began, he developed bilateral foot tingling. Over the following 5 days, weakness ascended rapidly from his feet to his hips. He is now unable to walk. Yesterday he noticed bilateral facial drooping and slurred speech. He has had dysphagia for thin liquids since this morning. As a physical therapist, he recognized the pattern immediately and came to the ED. He is short of breath when lying flat. He is alarmed and asking for IVIG. He has no bowel or bladder symptoms. No neck stiffness. No fever since his gastroenteritis resolved.

neurological_exam.additional: Speaks in short phrases; uses accessory muscles of respiration; cough weak. No paradoxical breathing.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Bilateral mild facial diplegia — both upper and lower face involved, forehead included. Mild dysarthria. Gag intact. No diplopia.
neurological_exam.gait: UNABLE TO WALK. Unable to stand without bilateral support.
neurological_exam.motor: Severe bilateral lower extremity weakness: hip flexion 2/5, knee extension 3/5, ankle dorsiflexion 2/5. Upper extremity: shoulder abduction 3+/5, elbow flexion 4/5, grip 4/5. Cannot rise from chair without arm support.
neurological_exam.reflexes: GLOBAL AREFLEXIA — absent bilaterally at all tendon reflexes including bilateral biceps, triceps, brachioradialis, patellar, Achilles.
neurological_exam.sensory: Bilateral distal glove-and-stocking paresthesias and numbness. Vibration absent at bilateral ankles and reduced at bilateral wrists.
